summary: Morgan County tower built at Centennial Church in 1950, per two Madison newspaper items; no source describes its later history or the site today.

events.note: Under construction in April 1950; reported complete, with radio installed, in a May 26, 1950 Madison Morgan County News item

evidence.supports: Georgia list places the Centennial tower in Morgan County at 33.584 N, 83.609 W, 778 ft
Eastern US Lookouts gives the agency as the Georgia Forestry Commission
April 1950 item: tower at Centennial Church under construction; Bulington hired to man it
evidence.quote: The tower at Centennial Church is under construction and Mr. V. E. Bulington of Brownwood has been employed to man it as soon as it is completed.

evidence.supports: May 1950 item: tower complete, radio installed, service planned for the following fall
evidence.quote: The lookout tower at Centennial Church has been completed and the radio has been installed. The tower will be put into operation next fall.

evidence.supports: NHLR Georgia index lists 29 registered lookouts; this tower is not among them
evidence.quote: There are 29 lookouts registered in Georgia.

corrections.why: No register we read lists this tower: the NHLR Georgia index lists 29 lookouts and does not name it. The only GFC code in our sources is gfc-019 on the Georgia towers list, which is a list code, not a register number

notes_for_editor: The built date rests on two Madison newspaper items as transcribed by Eastern US Lookouts; the originals were not read. The staffing item (V. E. Bulington) is a 1950 plan, so the story says he had been hired, not that he served. The brief's GFC US 19 register is not supported by any register read; removal is proposed. The gfc-019 code on the list is not explained there. Do not confuse with the Morgan (Bostwick) GFC tower, which the Eastern Morgan (Bostwick) page says was to be moved to Apalachee in 1957. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the April and May 1950 sentences in the story were reworded away from the transcribed items, which were confirmed on the Eastern page (April 6, 1950 and May 26, 1950 entries). The Georgia list prints no unit for elevation; feet is inferred from its Brasstown row (4735, which cannot be metres in Georgia). Confidence low.
